almighty.title: Almighty
almighty.note: It translates El Shaddai, a Hebrew title for God used most in the stories of the patriarchs and in Job. It describes who God is and what he can do, and it is not anyone's name.

bildad.title: Bildad
bildad.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
bildad.note: The second of Job's three friends to speak, a Shuhite. Like the others he insisted that Job's suffering had to come from hidden sin, and God later rebukes them for it.

eliphaz-2.title: Eliphaz
eliphaz-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
eliphaz-2.note: First and apparently oldest of Job's three friends, a Temanite. His speeches say suffering always comes from your own sin. At the end God rebukes him for not speaking rightly, as Job had.

job.title: Job
job.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
job.note: Uz was his country, and he was rich and righteous until God let Satan take his children, his wealth and his health to see whether his faith was only about the good life. He never curses God, but he does demand an answer. When God speaks from the whirlwind he gives no reason, only the size of creation, and Job goes quiet and gets back double.

naamathite.title: Naamathite
naamathite.note: The tag on Zophar, one of Job's three friends. Naamah, wherever it was, may have been in Arabia.

shiphi.title: Shiphi
shiphi.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shiphi.note: A Simeonite, father of Ziza. In Hezekiah's reign the tribe was pushing out into new pasture near Gedor, and Ziza was one of its leaders.

shuhite.title: Shuhite
shuhite.note: Bildad, one of Job's three friends, was a Shuhite. The word probably makes him a descendant of Shuah, Abraham's son by Keturah, whose people lived out in the Arabian desert.

temani.title: Temani
temani.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
temani.note: Teman was Esau's grandson, and his Edomite clan had a name for wisdom. This is the word for that clan, and it is what Eliphaz is called all through Job.

zophar.title: Zophar
zophar.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
zophar.note: The Naamathite, the third of Job's friends and the bluntest. He insisted Job's suffering proved hidden sin. God rebuked him for it.
